services.jsx:
Services

Six areas of specialization

The practice of Artur Witkowski covers six key areas of law. Each service is handled with full commitment, transparent pricing, and an individual approach to every client.

Practice Area

Criminal Defense

Comprehensive defense at every stage of criminal proceedings: from the first interrogation as a suspect through the court of first instance, appeals, and up to cassation before the Supreme Court. Includes representation of victims and early-stage evidence preservation during the investigation.

We handle cases involving offenses against life, health, property, sexual freedom, economic activity, and fiscal offenses. On-site dispatch to the scene of detention in Warsaw within 1 hour, available 24/7.

Comprehensive handling from PLN 12,000. Pricing.

Practice Area

Civil Litigation

Representation in property and non-property disputes. Preparation of statements of claim, defenses, interim remedies, and representation before courts of all instances. Full handling from initial consultation through judgment enforcement.

Contractual disputes, compensation claims, debt recovery, title recognition, possession protection, neighbor disputes, and commercial debt collection. Ongoing legal advisory for businesses.

From PLN 8,000. Pricing.

Practice Area

Family Law

Divorce, division of marital property, alimony enforcement, determination of child residence and contact arrangements, paternity establishment, and limitation of parental authority. Specialization in cross-border cases under EU Regulation 2016/1103.

Family matters require empathy and sensitivity. The initial consultation is devoted to thoroughly understanding the circumstances and selecting the optimal legal strategy.

From PLN 6,000. Pricing.

Practice Area

Corporate and Business Law

Legal advisory for businesses: drafting and negotiation of B2B contracts, corporate governance for LLCs and joint-stock companies, debt collection, commercial disputes, due diligence, restructuring, and defense before tax authorities and the Office of Competition and Consumer Protection (UOKiK).

Retainer-based legal services for businesses — ongoing access to advisory, contract database updates, and representation in disputes. From PLN 3,000 per month.

Retainer from PLN 3,000/month. Litigation from PLN 10,000.

Practice Area

Administrative Law

Challenges to administrative decisions: tax, construction, licensing, permitting, and environmental matters. Representation before the Voivodeship Administrative Court (WSA) and the Supreme Administrative Court (NSA). Assistance with obtaining concessions, licenses, and residence permits.

Appeal from PLN 2,000. WSA case from PLN 8,000.

Practice Area

European Court of Human Rights

An ECtHR application is the last instance of rights protection. We prepare applications concerning violations of the right to a fair trial (Article 6), private life (Article 8), prohibition of torture (Article 3), and liberty (Article 5). Deadline: 4 months. Representation in English.

Prospect analysis PLN 1,500. Application from PLN 15,000. Representation in Strasbourg from PLN 25,000.

Didn’t find your case type?

Every situation is different — get in touch and we will assess your case free of charge.

Contact Us

About the Firm

Attorney Artur Witkowski

Faculty of Law and Administration, Jagiellonian University (2001). Admitted to the Bar of the Warsaw District Bar Association (2004). Member of the Ethics Committee of the National Bar Council (2019–2023). Lecturer at the University of Warsaw (2016–2021).

Artur Witkowski is a Warsaw-based attorney with 22 years of professional experience. His career path is distinctive — having served on both sides of the aisle, prosecution and defense — which gives him a unique perspective in building effective litigation strategies.

He began his career in 2001 as a prosecutor trainee at the Warsaw Regional Prosecutor’s Office, where for two years he participated in investigations concerning economic crimes and corruption. This period provided him with deep insight into investigative psychology, interrogation tactics, and procedural nuances.

From 2003 to 2006, he completed his bar training with the Warsaw District Bar Association. Since 2006, he served as a partner at “Witkowski i Partnerzy” — a team of 5 lawyers with a B2B portfolio spanning the trade and construction sectors. From 2013, he was the managing partner at “LexFor”, expanding the firm’s scope to cross-border family law and ECtHR cases.

In 2018, he founded Payfair Law Office — a modern practice built on transparency, professional ethics, and an individual approach to each client. His philosophy: an attorney is like a physician — diagnose, treat, and monitor the outcome.

22 years of practice 2,000+ cases ECtHR PL / EN / DE

blog.jsx:
Publications

Insights from practice

Articles based on real court cases. Legal updates, commentary on judicial decisions, and practical guidance for clients and fellow practitioners.

Criminal Defense

Traffic accident involving a police officer — how the defense is built

Accidents involving law enforcement officers represent a distinct category of criminal cases. On one hand, there is heightened media and public scrutiny; on the other, specific internal procedures (both disciplinary and criminal) that must run in parallel. In this analysis, based on a real case from 2024, we examine the key legal aspects of constructing a defense line when the perpetrator is a police officer.

Key questions: the reliability of breathalyzer testing, the procedure for securing evidence at the scene, the issue of competent investigating authorities (National Prosecutor’s Office vs. regular prosecution), and rules governing disciplinary proceedings. In particular, we analyze the case law of the Supreme Court regarding Article 160 of the Polish Penal Code (failure to render assistance to a person in imminent danger) and Article 158 (causing a catastrophic road traffic accident resulting in death).

Author: attorney Artur Witkowski | Reading time: 8 min | Date: March 2026

Corporate Law

How to protect your business from unlawful actions by regulatory authorities

Regulatory inspections — by the Office of Competition and Consumer Protection (UOKiK), the Tax Authority (US), the National Labor Inspectorate (PIP), and the Chief Sanitary Inspectorate (GIS) — constitute a significant operational risk for every business in Poland. In this article, we analyze the most common errors committed by inspecting authorities: exceeding their competence, violating the right of defense, and delays in issuing decisions. We present a practical guide to available remedies: appeal to the superior authority, complaint to the administrative court, and a motion to stay the execution of a decision.

Particular attention is devoted to the provisions of the Code of Administrative Procedure of June 14, 1960 (Articles 127–137), as well as the case law of the Supreme Administrative Court regarding appeal deadlines and the possibility of securing a claim. Based on real cases from 2024–2025, we demonstrate how to properly prepare documentation for inspections and how to respond when violations are identified.

Author: attorney Artur Witkowski | Reading time: 10 min | Date: February 2026

Family Law

International divorce — EU Regulation 2016/1103 in court practice

When spouses from different countries decide to divorce, a fundamental question arises: which country’s law governs the division of property and alimony? The answer is provided by Regulation (EU) 2016/1103 of the European Parliament and of the Council, which regulates the matrimonial property regime in international situations. In Polish court practice, we are seeing a growing number of cases with a PL-DE, PL-UK, or PL-NL element.

We analyze the key mechanisms of the Regulation: choice of applicable law (Articles 8–16), scope of the applicable law (Articles 21–32), and recognition and enforcement of judgments (Articles 36–56). Drawing on the case law of the CJEU and Polish courts, we discuss typical problems: assets in multiple jurisdictions, marriage contracts from different legal systems, and cross-border alimony enforcement. Practical guidance for couples contemplating an international divorce.

Author: attorney Artur Witkowski | Reading time: 12 min | Date: January 2026

Privacy Policy

Last updated: July 1, 2026

1. Data Controller

The controller of your personal data is Payfair Law Office, based in Warsaw at ul. Nowy Świat 42, 00-029, KRS: 0000000000, NIP: 0000000000, email: biuro@payfair.pl (hereinafter: “the Firm” or “we”). For matters relating to personal data protection, you may contact us at biuro@payfair.pl or by registered mail at our registered address.

2. What data we collect

We collect personal data provided in the contact form: first name, last name, phone number, email address, subject, and message content. Additionally, we process IP address, browser type, operating system, pages visited, and time and date of visit — as part of website analytics (Plausible service, GDPR-compliant without the use of cookies).

3. Purpose and legal basis for processing

Contact form data is processed in order to respond to your inquiry (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR — performance of a contract or steps taken at your request before entering into a contract). Analytics data is processed on the basis of the controller’s legitimate interest (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR) — improving website functionality.

4. Data recipients

Your data is not shared with third parties, except for service providers we use to operate the website (Vercel hosting, Plausible analytics, Resend email). All recipients are GDPR-compliant and process data on the basis of data processing agreements.

5. Cookies

The website uses technically necessary (session) cookies for proper functioning. We do not use marketing or analytics cookies that track users. Analytics are provided by Plausible (cookie-free, GDPR-compliant). The cookie banner is displayed only on the first visit — your choice must be confirmed.

6. Your rights

Under the GDPR, you have the right to: access your data (Art. 15), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17), restriction of processing (Art. 18), data portability (Art. 20), and objection (Art. 21). To exercise your rights, contact us at biuro@payfair.pl. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (ul. Stawki 2, 00-193 Warsaw).

7. Retention period

Contact form data is retained for 12 months from the last contact, after which it is automatically deleted. Analytics data is retained for 26 months in accordance with Plausible’s data retention policy. Data processed in the context of a legal services engagement is retained for the duration of the applicable limitation period.

faq.jsx:
FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does the first consultation cost?
Telephone (up to 30 min) — PLN 300. In-office (1 hour) — PLN 500. Written opinion — from PLN 500/page. For criminal matters (detention), the first telephone consultation is free of charge.

Which cities do you handle cases in?
Main office in Warsaw. Cases handled across all of Poland — we travel to any city. For criminal matters, emergency dispatch within 1 hour in Warsaw, 3–6 hours in other cities.

What languages do you serve clients in?
Polish, English, and German. Documents are prepared in the language of the relevant jurisdiction. Where needed, we collaborate with sworn translators.

Do you guarantee the outcome of a case?
Professional ethics prohibit guaranteeing outcomes. After reviewing your documents, I assess the prospects in percentage terms and communicate them honestly. If the prospects are doubtful, I propose alternative strategies.

How does payment work?
Costs are agreed upon in a written engagement before any work begins. PLN, EUR, or USD at the NBP mid-market rate. For matters exceeding PLN 10,000 — installment plan up to 6 months. Bank transfer, card, or cash.

Do you represent clients before the ECtHR?
Yes. Prospect analysis — PLN 1,500. Application — from PLN 15,000. Representation in Strasbourg — from PLN 25,000. Application deadline: 4 months from the final domestic court decision.

What should I do if I’ve been detained?
1) Do not make any statements without an attorney. 2) Demand to see an attorney (it is your right). 3) Call +48 22 555 00 00 — I will be on-site within 1 hour in Warsaw. 4) Do not sign anything without legal counsel.
